items.title: Cops probing claims Hadi was offered US backing to topple BN govt
items.summary: He said the case was being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. "Investigation under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code involves an offence relating to statements that could cause public alarm and, upon conviction, carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both. "Investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 involves the improper use of network facilities or network services.

items.title: 4-month-old baby dies after being found unconscious at nursery
items.summary: DUNGUN: A four-month-old baby girl died after she was found unconscious at a nursery in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah here yesterday. Dungun district police chief Superintendent Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the baby was pronounced dead at Dungun Hospital at about 12.45pm. He said police received a report on the incident at 3.41pm.

items.title: Malaysia, Thailand to step up coordination on border security, smuggling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Thailand will streamline coordination among agencies from both countries, particularly on security and development in border areas, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said the matter was among the issues discussed during his meeting with Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow today, with both sides seeking to better coordinate existing cooperation, including efforts to combat smuggling. "Both Malaysia and Thailand suffer losses, as goods are smuggled into Thailand, just as goods are smuggled from Thailand into Malaysia," he told a press conference after hosting a luncheon for his Thai counterpart in conjunction with Sihasak's two-day working visit to Malaysia.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for six states until 1am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas in six states until 1am today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states involved are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kedah, the affected areas are Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they are Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Larut Matang and Selama.

items.title: Freedom of Information Bill committee to hold National Townhall on Sept 28
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the committee agreed to hold the session after considering views and feedback from stakeholders. She said the townhall would help ensure key issues concerning the Bill's framework were thoroughly considered before the committee finalised its recommendations and views. Azalina also chaired the Third Meeting of the Parliamentary Special Select Committee on the Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill 2026.

items.title: 59 KLIA flights cancelled as Indonesia closes airspace over volcanic eruption
items.summary: Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) senior general manager Hasman Abd Muhimim said 6,279 passengers were affected by the cancellations. On flights scheduled for tomorrow, Hasman said MAHB had so far only received notifications of cancellations for today. "Passengers scheduled to fly tomorrow should contact their respective airlines for the latest information and to determine their next flight arrangements," he said.

items.title: Fitch downgrades Genting ratings
items.summary: "This is compounded by a slower-than-expected earnings ramp-up at Genting New York LLC because of high start-up operating costs, as well as a more gradual recovery across Genting's other gaming operations," it said. Genting New York's capex will likely remain high at an average of about US$800 million per year over the medium term. "We expect Genting New York's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (ebitda) to increase to US$208 million in 2026 as the casino ramps up.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 7, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's biggest stories: Heavier sentences Police have proposed amendments to outdated laws and tougher penalties, including rotan, for online scammers. Found The six hikers reported missing while taking part in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Mount Gerah, Kelantan, have been found safe, police confirmed today. Inquiry report The investigation into the roller coaster accident at Sunway Lagoon in Subang Jaya is expected to take at least three to four months to complete, said Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar.

items.title: Taska worker remanded 6 days over alleged rough treatment of 2-year-old
items.summary: Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the woman was detained following a police report lodged by the girl's 29-year-old mother on Sept 5. Police had earlier detected a social media post about the alleged incident before the girl's mother lodged a formal report. Police are continuing their investigations.

items.title: MNHB unit in JV with Pembinaan Tajri for RM67mil TNB cable installation contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's (MNHB) wholly owned unit, MN Utilities Engineering Sdn Bhd (MNUE) and Pembinaan Tajri Sdn Bhd (PTSB) has bagged a contract for the installation of a new 275 kilovolt (kV) cable from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB). The contract, worth RM67.31 million, was secured via an unincorporated joint-venture (JV) arrangement between MNUE and PTSB. "Both MNUE and PTSB have agreed to collaborate and work together via an unincorporated JV for the contract," it added.

items.title: Leapmotor EVs go local
items.summary: The locally assembled models will be available through authorised Leapmotor dealers nationwide. The company said Leapmotor and Stellantis operate under a unified global compliance framework to maintain consistent manufacturing standards across locally assembled vehicles. The locally assembled C10 is offered with two new exterior colours — Violet and Lightning White — alongside Canopy Grey and Glazed Green.

items.title: Elderly man who allegedly slashed wife over TV volume remanded 4 days
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI:An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife's right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here on Saturday has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations. Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at 9.30pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high. He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: MAHB: 41 flights to Jakarta cancelled following Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: The airport operator said that Penang International Airport recorded seven cancellations, followed by Subang Airport with two, while Kuching International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport recorded one cancellation each. No cancellations were recorded at Kota Bharu Airport. The cancellations followed the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption affected flight operations.

items.title: Cops hunt 10 men after 2 Shah Alam brawls, 1 death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police are hunting 10 men believed to be involved in two separate group fights here last month, one of which resulted in a death. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the men, aged between 23 and 46, were being sought to assist investigations into separate incidents in Alam Megah on Aug 25 and Taman Sri Muda on Aug 14. He said a 23-year-old man died in the group fight in Alam Megah and was found to have six previous records involving drug offences.

items.title: Four-month old baby dies after found unconscious at Dungun childcare centre
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 7 — A four-month-old baby girl died after being found unconscious at a childcare centre in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah (AMBS) near here today. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the incident at 3.41 pm. Nik Ab Halim said medical personnel at the hospital conducted examinations and resuscitation efforts, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but the baby was pronounced dead at about 12.45 pm.

items.title: Gas Malaysia, Petronas Gas team up on potential Yan pipeline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gas Malaysia Bhd has signed a joint study and collaboration agreement with Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) to develop an onshore lateral pipeline to facilitate the regasification terminal project in Yan, Kedah. Gas Malaysia, in a filing with Bursa Malaysia, said the agreement sets out a framework for both parties to conduct a feasibility study and related activities for the proposed lateral pipeline. "The feasibility study is intended to assess the technical, operational and commercial viability of the proposed pipeline interconnection, including engineering design, land acquisition requirements and other technical assessments required to support PetGas confirmation on the proposed interconnection.

items.title: Hextar Portfolio raises Hextar Retail stake, triggers mandatory offer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Portfolio Sdn Bhd's conditional voluntary takeover offer for Hextar Retail Bhd has turned into a mandatory offer after acquiring an additional 4.82 per cent stake. Hextar Portfolio bought an additional 22.41 million shares on the open market, raising its stake in Hextar Retail to about 35.4 per cent. Following the acquisition, Hextar Portfolio now holds 164.7 million shares in Hextar Retail, according to an announcement made through RHB Investment Bank Bhd.

items.title: Police: Six missing Gunung Trans Gerah hikers contacted, safe for now
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 7 — Six individuals, including two children, who were reported missing while trekking along the Gunung Trans Gerah trail in Lojing, Gua Musang, have managed to make contact this afternoon and reported that they are safe. Gerik police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said information regarding the group’s condition was received at about 5.30 pm today after a family member managed to contact one of the mountain guides accompanying the group. Abdul Samad said the method for extracting the group - whether by land or air - will be determined based on their condition and location after the SAR team manages to meet the victims.

items.title: Malaysians urged to register on Foreign Ministry’s E-Konsular as precaution, though not mandatory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Recent developments around the world, arising from natural disasters and geopolitical situations, have increased the need for Malaysians to register with the Foreign Affairs Ministry’s e-Konsular system to provide information on their whereabouts. For instance, when major floods occurred in Nepal last month, information on Malaysians there was obtained only from their relatives back home and travel agencies used by Malaysians travelling to the country. According to the ekonsular.kln.gov.my website, the registration is intended to systematically record the whereabouts of Malaysians overseas.

items.title: Malaysia, Australia team up on drones to boost maritime surveillance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Australia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) to expand maritime surveillance and enforcement capabilities across the country's vast waters. The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) said the cooperation would leverage Australia's expertise in drone technology and extensive maritime operational experience, alongside Malaysia's understanding of its maritime environment and enforcement requirements. MMEA director-general Maritime Admiral Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said the technology could serve as a force multiplier by providing aerial surveillance support and extending the agency's coverage of maritime areas.

items.title: Malaysia deploying DNA experts to identify disaster victims, pending Nepal’s go-ahead
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia had submitted a request to deploy the experts, with the DNA identification process expected to begin after search and rescue (SAR) operations conclude. He said the expertise was needed to match DNA samples taken from recovered bodies with samples provided by the families of Malaysian citizens who remain missing. “We need DNA to match against the DNA samples from the families of the Malaysian citizens.

items.title: HR-V spins 3 times in chain-reaction crash, 4 injured
items.summary: The Honda HR-V then spun three times before crashing into a parked Perodua Alza and the fence of a roadside house. "The Honda HR-V then spun three times before heading towards my house and crashing into the parked Perodua Alza. The fence of my house was also damaged.

items.title: Malaysia's construction upcycle: Opportunities across the field
items.summary: MALAYSIA's construction sector is enjoying something it has not experienced consistently for many years: sustained momentum. Construction sector's economic output as measured by gross domestic product (GDP) at current prices reached RM86.9 billion in 2025, up 11.3 per cent from the preceding year, and the momentum has carried into 2026. In the first half of this year, construction sector's GDP reached RM45.6 billion, representing year-on-year (y-o-y)growth of 8.5 per cent.

items.title: Police, Media Prima strengthen strategic collaboration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police and Media Prima Bhd have strengthened their strategic collaboration through the PDRM-Media Prima Strategic Communication Collaboration Programme to boost mutual understanding and curb the spread of false news. Inspector-General of Police, Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, said police value its cooperation with the media, which it regards as the "eyes and ears" of the community, with the police serving as the bulwark of the rule of law. Also present were Media Prima Group Chairman Datuk Seri (Dr) Syed Hussian Aljunid; Media Prima News and Current Affairs Group Managing Editor Jasbant Singh; and Datuk Farrah Naz Abdul Karim, who is Media Prima NCA Deputy Group Managing Editor and New Straits Times Group Editor.

items.title: Ringgit ends marginally lower against US dollar after strong US jobs data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed slightly lower on Monday after the United States posted strong non-farm payrolls (NFP) data and ahead of a US inflation report later this week. The US NFP data last Friday came in at 162,000 in August, well above the consensus forecast of 55,000. At 6pm, the ringgit inched down to 4.0440/0485 against the US dollar from last Friday's close of 4.0425/0465.

items.title: Vestland unit bags RM263.7mil job in Kelantan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd's unit Vestland Infra Sdn Bhd has been awarded a contract by Johnson Fluid Engineering Sdn Bhd to build a dual-function sheet pile wall and bridge works in Kelantan valued at RM263.7 million. Vestland joint managing director Datuk Liew Foo Heen said this is its sixth contract win for the year and represents its strategic expansion into flood mitigation and infrastructure development. The latest contract brings Vestland's contract wins for this year to RM1.1 billion and strengthens its total outstanding order book to RM1.5 billion.

items.title: Former TV station assistant director jailed six months over RM28,000 bribes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A former assistant director of a television station was sentenced to six months' jail and fined RM20,000 by the Shah Alam Sessions Court after being found guilty of two charges of receiving RM28,000 seven years ago. He also ordered her to servce six months in jail for each charge if she failed to pay the fine. The court also found that the use of a third-party account to make the payment indicated an attempt to conceal the offence.

items.title: Elderly man remanded four days for slashing wife’s hand
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 7 — An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife’s right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here today has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations. Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at about 9.30 pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high. He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: On a Kyiv maternity ward, babies are born during air raids
items.summary: THE air raid alert in Kyiv was live, warning of approaching Russian jet-propelled drones, but fortunately there were no explosions nearby during the final phase of Alyona Bohatyrenko's labour. "I gave birth during an air alert!" Doctors at Kyiv City Maternity Hospital No.

items.title: Anak Krakatau volcanic ash hampers efforts to induce rain, further eruptions possible
items.summary: JAKARTA: Efforts to induce rain following eruptions at Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau are being hampered by volcanic ash, as authorities warned that further eruptions could occur at any time amid high seismic activity. The agency said it continued to closely monitor the volcano through the Anak Krakatau Volcano Observation Posts in Pasauran, Banten, and Kalianda, Lampung. He said BNPB was considering three airports as bases for conducting the OMC: Pondok Cabe Airport near Jakarta once conditions allowed, Kertajati International Airport in West Java or Ahmad Yani International Airport in Semarang, Central Java.

items.title: Volcanic ash eases, but Indonesian airports remains closed
items.summary: JAKARTA: Volcanic ash conditions around several Indonesian airports showed signs of improvement, with tests at four airports finding no ash at ground level. Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said four consecutive ground-level tests at Soekarno-Hatta had returned negative for volcanic ash, but authorities were holding off reopening Indonesia's main international gateway until they were satisfied that conditions were safe. He said eight airports affected by Anak Krakatau's volcanic ash had initially been temporarily closed, with Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, South Sumatra, reopening at 9am today after an assessment found it was no longer affected.

items.title: More than 1,000 open burning cases recorded in Pahang this year
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang recorded a significant increase in open burning cases in the first eight months of this year, with 1,003 cases reported compared to 658 during the same period last year. Razam Taja cautioned the public against taking open burning incidents lightly, particularly during dry conditions. "The public should refrain from open burning, particularly from burning rubbish, dry leaves, overgrown bushes or agricultural waste.

items.title: Police tracking down 10 suspects to assist in murder, gang fight in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — Police are tracking down 10 men to assist in the investigation of two separate fight cases in Taman Alam Megah and Taman Sri Muda here last month. Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said of that number, seven men are wanted to assist in the investigation of a fight in Taman Alam Megah that resulted in the death of a 23-year-old local man on Aug 25. He said following both cases, police conducted a series of raids in Shah Alam, as well as Lenga and Iskandar Puteri, Johor, between Aug 14 and 28.

items.title: 3 Sarawak areas record very unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today. Meanwhile, 37 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings, ranging from 106 to 196. Nilai (162), Seremban (160) and Port Dickson (120) in Negri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy air quality.

items.title: 17ha peatland blaze in Pengerang expected to take 2 days to put out
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters battling a peatland blaze along the Sebana Cove-Punggai bypass in Pengerang are expected to need another two days to completely extinguish the fire, which has burned 17 hectares. Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said firefighters had so far put out flames over 10 hectares of the affected area. "The fire has spread to the other side of the road, bringing the total area affected to 17 hectares.

items.title: Singapore's high ministerial salaries under scrutiny in parliament this week
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Top ministers in Singapore will discuss ministerial salaries in parliament on Tuesday, a sensitive and closely watched topic in the city-state, where political office comes with high rates of pay in order to attract talent and deter graft. Singapore pays its political leaders the highest salary in the world, with a junior minister taking home S$1.1 million (US$868,056) annually and the prime minister earning S$2.2 million (US$1.74 million) a year. In comparison, the British prime minister makes US$230,000 while President Donald Trump earns US$400,000.

items.title: Housing Ministry: Check Teduh to check project, developer information before buying property
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The public, particularly prospective homebuyers, are encouraged to check information on developers and housing projects through the TEDUH portal and mobile application before making a purchase decision to reduce the risk of encountering problems later. The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said TEDUH, developed by the National Housing Department (JPN), is a one-stop platform providing access to information such as developers’ licence status, advertising permit and developer’s licence (APDL), project progress and information related to private housing projects. The public can access the TEDUH Portal via teduh.kpkt.gov.my or use the TEDUH mobile application.

items.title: Over 26,000 new undergraduates to benefit from RM1,500 PTPTN advance payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) continues to strengthen the nation’s higher education empowerment agenda by offering Loan Advance Payments (WPP) totaling RM1,500 to eligible new students to help cover part of the initial preparation costs for admission to public universities and polytechnics. In a statement, PTPTN said the RM39.7 million scheme benefits 26,457 students entering bachelor’s degree programmes at public universities and polytechnics for the September 2026 intake. “The WPP is available to Malaysian citizens who opted into the scheme when applying to public higher education institutions via UPUOnline or university websites.

items.title: Malaysia rail link: ECRL passenger fares to be known by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Passenger fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) have not been finalised and an official announcement will be made by the end of this year, said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL). MRL said in a statement on the ECRL Facebook page today that a recently recirculated information on social media regarding the passenger fares is inaccurate and has never been verified by any authority. The company said the official passenger fares for the ECRL will only be announced by the Ministry of Transport Malaysia once the relevant evaluation and approval processes are finalised.

items.title: Minden air quality hits unhealthy level as API rises to 142, says Penang exco
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — Air quality in parts of Penang island reached an unhealthy level today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading climbing to 142 at 3pm. Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the Minden air-quality monitoring station on the island began recording unhealthy readings at 9am. Sundarajoo said Penang’s air quality had generally remained at good to moderate levels between September 4 and 6.

items.title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS. PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS. “So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.

items.title: Police: Missing hikers said they were in good condition when speaking to family on Tuesday
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 7 —Police said the six hikers, who are feared missing on Gunung Trans Gerah in Kelantan, were in good condition when they last contacted their family members on Tuesday (Sept 1), before continuing their journey towards Perak. District police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the group last contacted their family at 7.47 am that day. “The group began their hike on Aug 29 from the Pos Dakoh area in Gua Musang, Kelantan, and were expected to make their way out via Pos Kemar, Perak on Sept 3.

items.title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case. He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.

items.title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday. Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend. “Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.

items.title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
items.summary: Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur. “In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.

items.title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election. The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported. His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.

items.title: RM10,000 and a detour via Surabaya: Malaysian family stranded in Indonesia scrambles to get home after ash cloud cancels flights
items.summary: Wan Nor Ridani, 29, said his family had decided to travel by car to Surabaya before flying to Senai, Johor, as direct flights from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur were sold out, Berita Harian reported today. The family had already bought new tickets from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur for tomorrow, but decided not to risk another cancellation as airport operations remained subject to intermittent closures. From Senai, we will continue to Kuala Lumpur because all direct flights to Kuala Lumpur are already sold out,” he said.

items.title: Appeals court reserves decision on bid to stay committal proceedings against former undang Mubarak, five others
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The Court of Appeal reserved its decision on an application by six individuals, including former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, to stay the committal proceedings against them pending disposal of their appeal. The court also extended the ad interim stay of the committal proceedings granted to the six individuals until a decision is made on their stay application. A different three-man bench of the Court of Appeal had granted the ad interim stay on July 29 pending today’s hearing on the stay application.

items.title: Missing hiking family in Kelantan mountains never stayed out more than a day, says grandpa — now it’s been four, maybe without food
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The silence from his son’s family has left Wan Zairudin Wan Ismail fearing that something may have gone wrong during their hike through the Kelantan forest. His son Wan Ahmad Aslam, 39, daughter-in-law Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, grandchildren Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and their two mountain guides have been missing since failing to emerge from the forest as scheduled last Thursday. Wan Zairudin lodged a police report at the Bukit Jelutong police station in Shah Alam two days ago.

items.title: Police confirm RM27.5m drug syndicate crippled with main suspect shot dead
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police’s (PDRM) Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) crippled a drug processing syndicate suspected of producing Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth a total of RM27.5 million in this district and Kuala Lumpur in Op Thrips yesterday. He said the house rented by the suspect had been used as a laboratory to process the drugs since early this year, adding that police seized suspected MDMA comprising 64.49 kilogrammes (kg) of liquid, 5.2kg of drug lumps, 7.9kg of drug pills, 104.8kg of drug powder, as well as various drug-processing equipment. Hussein said the main suspect was also wanted under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, in addition to having a previous criminal record under Section 448 of the Penal Code.

items.title: Shahrir Samad and Tommy Thomas discussing possible resolution of civil suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The High Court today adjourned proceedings in the civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, and two others, to facilitate settlement negotiations among the parties. Judge Gan Techiong ordered the adjournment after Shahrir’s counsel Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin informed the court that his client and the defendants were discussing a possible resolution of the matter. Shahrir had been scheduled to continue giving his testimony in the matter today.

items.title: Hadi ready to face police over US ‘topple govt’ claim, says aide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang is expected to give a statement to police after Bukit Aman contacted him over his claim that the United States sought to help topple the Malaysian government before the 2018 general election. Hadi’s political secretary Syahir Sulaiman said the PAS president was ready to cooperate, although no date has been fixed for his statement, Berita Harian reported today. “Yes, Bukit Aman has contacted us.

items.title: No new wage target, but economy minister says govt wants greater transparency in salary offers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Economy Ministry is looking at ways to make salary offers more transparent and equitable, rather than setting an absolute wage target. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said wage growth was important to ensure the benefits of economic growth were felt by the people. Akmal said greater transparency was needed in salary offers to ensure workers received fairer returns for their contributions.

items.title: Two women remanded over alleged child mistreatment at Pahang nurseries
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 7 — Two women have been remanded for six days to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres in Kuantan and Temerloh. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the two nursery staff, aged 31 and 26, were remanded for six days until Saturday (Sept 12) following applications by police at the Kuantan and Temerloh Magistrates’ Courts. Meanwhile, Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received a report from the child’s 29-year-old mother at about 6 pm yesterday over allegations that her two-year-old daughter had been mistreated by a nanny at a nursery near Temerloh.

items.title: Four days overdue, rescuers mount land, air and water search for six hikers in Kelantan mountains
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 7 — Rescue teams are being mobilised by water, land and air in preparation for a search and rescue (SAR) operation for six individuals feared missing while hiking at Gunung Trans Gerah in Lojing, Kelantan. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (better known by its Malay initials JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received information about the missing two mountain guides and four family members yesterday afternoon, prompting discussions with the JBPM headquarters’ operations division on the search plan. He said three boats from the Trojan Jetty in Gerik would transport eight members of the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Team and five fire and rescue mountain guides by water to Pos Kemar.

items.title: Anthony Loke: Steps taken to strengthen checks on aviation personnel including pilots and cabin crew
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) are taking steps to strengthen checks on pilots, cabin crew and other aviation personnel following the case involving a Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilot linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate. Loke said MOT would definitely provide full cooperation to police, including access to airport facilities and any information or personnel required for the investigation. “The investigation is under the police.

items.title: Communications minister: Nadi-PKD synergy to optimise government resources, boost public service delivery
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Sept 7 — Efforts to strengthen collaboration between the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) and Rural Community Centres (PKD) under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) reflect the government’s focus on synergy, resource optimisation and better public service delivery. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Nadi had evolved beyond providing computers and Internet access to become community information and empowerment hubs connecting people with skills, opportunities and government services. Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.

items.title: Ex-Felda general manager under five-day remand as MACC digs into KL land deal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A former Felda general manager has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur and the sale of land owned by the statutory body. Yesterday, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009. Last week, MACC opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).

items.title: Inquest told father never consulted over Zara’s autopsy
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 7 — The Coroner’s Court heard today that the father of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was never asked for his consent regarding an autopsy on his daughter. Testifying before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said a doctor confirmed Zara's death in his presence at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I (HQE I) on July 17, 2025. Mahathir told the court that a attending female doctor informed him Zara was in critical condition with a broken leg and severe internal bleeding in her brain, lungs, and kidneys, adding that she would remain permanently comatose if she survived.
